most magnum loads are bullshit...they have lots of shot in them, but that sacrifices velocity (only so much room in the shell).

I once thought this way, but during a certain duck hunt I started noticing things...for one thing too high of a percentage of birds were hit by flying off the property and then falling (this meant I would be risking some trouble if I tresspassed on another property to retrieve my kill)...I was also actually seeing/hearing birds being hit but still flying away (most likely to die a slow death)...both of these scenarios result in a waste of meat and a waste of a life taken (as a side note I used the feathers many times to tie flies with to both sell and use for my own stash)...now, here I am using buffered Winchester Super-X 2 3/4" mags and thinking WTF is up? coincidentally my father had just gotten set up for hand loading, so I looked in the ol' "whatever" book of loads and decided I was going to go for maximum velocity (having already taken enough math classes to know what this meant) as opposed to lots of lead. what I ended up with was a load with 1 3/8 oz of shot and some amount of slow burning powder (keeps on burning while the shot is traveling down the barrel and actually increases muzzle velocity...on the negative side not all gets burned and this tends to clog up the gun especially in a nice rain storm) which I forget...this load was known for blowing primers out the end sometimes. a very deadly load which solved my problem of hitting ducks/geese yet not dropping them...
